habitat: Pairs in valleys with cliffs or rocks, or grassland with rock outcrops and trees. It generally does not enter cities.
summary: An uncommon resident. A large, stocky brownish owl with prominent ear tufts, orange-yellow eyes and heavily blotched underparts with bold barring. The immature's eyes are orange. The call is HU-hu-hu or HU-hu, and the alarm is wak-wak. Birds in Zimbabwe and Mozambique are larger than the southern race. No Kemp estimate is stored.

similar.note: Spotted Eagle-Owl is smaller, with pale yellow eyes, fine barring, lighter blotching and smaller feet.

head.pattern: Prominent ear tufts. The eyes are orange on the identification line and orange-yellow in the description. The immature's eyes are orange.

upperparts.pattern: Dark brown above. The description calls the bird brownish.

underparts.pattern: Buffy underparts with brown and white blotching, heavily blotched, and bold barring.

viewNotes.note: Orange-yellow eyes and prominent ear tufts. The identification line says orange eyes.
Brownish and stocky, with heavily blotched underparts.
The underside in flight is not described.

calls.description: The call is 'HU-hu-hu' or 'HU-hu', with the emphasis on the first syllable. The alarm is 'wak-wak'. No grade A recording was found. The selected file is a grade B call from the Eastern Cape. The filename is XC808452-Cape-Eagle-owl-brilliant.mp3.

research.note: Newman calls it an uncommon resident, and Avibase does not mark it rare, so all twelve months are listed. The eyes are orange and orange-yellow, so no single iris colour is stored. No grade A recording was found. No Kruger photograph was found. No Kemp estimate is stored.

population.notes: No sourced Kruger estimate is currently available; taxonomy or later records require separate research.
